chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:

A man appointed his children as executors, and among them were adults who had reached maturity and among them were minors. Is it permissible for the adults to carry out the bequest and pay his debt to the one who established it against the deceased through just witnesses before the minors reach maturity?
So he عليه السلام wrote: "It is upon the adult children to pay their father's debt and not withhold it on account of that."

key_terms.أَوْصَى: he made a bequest or appointed executors
key_terms.دَيْنَهُ: his debt owed by the deceased
key_terms.كِبَارٌ: adult children who have reached maturity
key_terms.يَحْبِسُوهُ: to hold it back or delay payment

ai.seo_question: Can adult heirs or executors pay a deceased father's proven debts before minor heirs come of age?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the execution of a deceased father's bequest when some of his appointed children are adults and others are minors. Imam al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام states that the adult children must settle their father's established debts without delaying until the minors reach maturity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5487 - Muhammad bin Al-Hasan Al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, wrote to Abu Muhammad Imam Hasan ibn Ali Al-Askari (as)

about a man who made his children the  executors of his will, among them adults who are mature and minors who are not mature yet.
He asked if it was permissible for the adults to execute the will and settle their father's debts, proven against the deceased by trustworthy witnesses, before the minors reached maturity.
Abu Muhammad (as) replied: "It is obligatory upon the adult children to settle their father's debts and not delay this obligation."
